events.title: Teen Hacks: AI/ML for Cybersecurity, Healthcare & Sustainability

cases.refreshed: Do you want to showcase your programming skills? Do you want to compete for prizes while gaining valuable teamwork skills? Join us for a Hackathon led by Anish Roy and the team of the AI/ML Boot Camp series. The event will be held at the King Library and is jointly hosted by the SJSU University Library and the San José Public Library. This exciting event is open to all middle and high school students eager to collaborate on coding projects and connect with like-minded peers. Compete for prizes and take advantage of this unique opportunity to grow and learn. The challenge for the hackathon is Artificial Intelligence for Social Good. Create an AI-based program targeted at a global issue, such as Cybersecurity, Healthcare, or Sustainability. This prompt is meant to be loose, giving you and your team as much creative freedom as possible. Schedule 9:00-9:30 Team formation 9:30-12:45 Coding (3 hours 15 minutes) 12.45-1:15 Lunch 1:15-2:45 Coding & presentation prep (1 hour 30 minutes) 2:45-4:30 Presentation, Judging 4:30-4:50 Award ceremony 4:50-5:00 Wrap up Important information: Lunch will be provided. Please bring your own laptop or tablet and its charger.

events.title: Sparksteam Robotics Program: Learn, Build, Code, Play with Robots

In this 1.5-hour workshop, students will learn the basics of building and programming robots using LEGO robotics kits. Sparksteam will provide Robotics Kits and laptops that will be used for programming the robots. We just need enthusiastic kids! The program is geared toward grades 2-5. Free. Everyone has something to contribute! Construye comunidad con personas de diferentes antecedentes lingüísticos y culturales. ¡Todos tienen algo que aportar! In this program, Spanish-proficient participants with limited English skills will share their linguistic and cultural knowledge with English-proficient participants with limited Spanish skills and vice-versa to create a mutually enriching learning experience. Free. Registration requested but not required.

events.title: Intermediate Mass Black Holes; Meteor Showers or Space Debris?

cases.refreshed: Lecture 1: Understanding how supermassive black holes grow offers key clues to how galaxies evolve, but their "missing link"—intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs)—remains elusive. Because small, blue compact dwarf galaxies cannot host supermassive monsters, they are prime hunting grounds for IMBHs. In this talk, we explore how changes in visible gas emission lines over nearly two decades can reveal these hidden engines, highlighting recent Magellan Spectrograph observations of dwarf galaxy J1143 that point to an accreting intermediate-mass black hole at its core. Delivered by Kiera Aston. Lecture 2: Gorgeous meteor showers streaking across the zenith, or space trash entering our atmosphere? The 21st century's growing "space environment" problem is beginning to take center stage. Space debris, artificial spacecraft and objects that have ceased functioning, are accumulating in Low Earth Orbit at an unprecedented rate. We are developing a global space debris monitoring network using ground-based observations. At the core of the system is a three-channel multispectral camera designed to detect the aluminum emission line in the near-UV spectrum, providing a distinctive signature for identifying space debris as it reenters Earth's atmosphere. Delivered by Alice Zou. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.

events.title: Beyond the Spotlight: One Life. Multiple Passions. Endless Possibilities

cases.refreshed: In this inspiring talk with professionals, we explore how passion for the performing arts can coexist with a primary career. Can you be a professional by day and a performer by choice? What does it look like when theater becomes more than a hobby without becoming your full-time profession? Through personal stories, practical insights, and thoughtful conversation, this event invites participants to rethink traditional career paths, make space for creativity, and redefine what success can look like. We will discuss how aspiring performers can balance education, professional goals, personal responsibilities, and their love for the stage. Join us for a thought-provoking discussion on pursuing Performing Arts and Theater as a Parallel Career Path: an exploration of passion, purpose, possibility, and the courage to embrace more than one professional identity. Carla Pantoja Carla, born and raised in the South Bay, is an actor, fight director, teaching artist, intimacy director, and mom of two. She has been a Resident Artist of San Francisco Shakespeare Festival since 2014 and recently served as Director of Vision for the 2021 Free Shakespeare in the Park production of Pericles, Prince of Tyre, directing episodes 2 and 4. In 2020, she was in the acting company at Oregon Shakespeare Festival, returning in 2022 as the festival's first female fight director. Carla is an associate instructor for Dueling Arts International and serves on their governing body as President. She is also a proud member of Making Good Trouble, an anti-racist training cohort based in the Bay Area. Carla has directed SF Shakes Shakespeare on Tour production of Romeo and Juliet and Comedy of Errors and Assistant Directed the 2017 Free Shakespeare in the Park production of Hamlet. She played Paulina in Free Shakespeare in the Park's The Winter's Tale, Tybalt in Romeo and Juliet, and Kate in The Taming of the Shrew. She's performed with Cal Shakes, Shotgun Players, Crowded Fire, Playground, Lorraine Hansberry Theatre, and the SF Mime Troupe in the Bay Area to name a few. Vinay Pande Vinay Pande is a Silicon Valley technology leader and a passionate theatre artist who brings together the worlds of innovation and performing arts. Originally from Mumbai, India, Vinay holds a degree in Instrumentation Engineering and began his career in telecommunications, where he was part of the core team that developed India's first satellite-based mission-critical voice, data, and video network for the Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO). He later worked as a researcher at the prestigious Bell Labs and holds 15 technology patents, and co-authored technical publications and books. Today, he serves as a Principal Architect at a leading technology company in Silicon Valley. Beyond his technology career, Vinay has nurtured a deep passion for the performing arts for over a decade, actively pursuing theatre, acting, and singing across Marathi and Hindi productions. From bringing diverse characters to life on stage to engaging audiences as a Radio Jockey and event host, he thrives on the energy of live performance and the magic of storytelling. For Vinay, technology may be his profession, but the stage is where his creative spirit truly comes alive. Sowmya Renukuntla Sowmya is a Bay Area native and recent graduate from Santa Clara University, where she studied Business and worked directly with Admission Counselors for four years. Since graduating, she has been working full-time at Levi Strauss & Co. On the Corporate Insights team and is a part-time college counselor. Sponsored by the Cupertino Library Foundation. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
